messages.subject: ignoring imported data packages
parts:
I've got a project that requires dplyr, which works fine, but dplyr imports a couple of data packages (Lahman, hflights) that probably ought to be suggested instead. Is there a way to tell Packrat not to install those two packages, even though it thinks it should? 

 -Harlan

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: ignoring imported data packages
parts:
Sorry, there isn't a mechanism for this in packrat. An alternative:

Turn on the global cache. This installs packages into one 'global' area, and symlinks them into projects as needed, so that even if you have multiple projects using (some version of) dplyr, they will all grab the same (single) version from the cache. Do this with:

    packrat::set_opts(use.cache = TRUE)

then run 'packrat::snapshot()' and 'packrat::restore()' to migrate any project packages to the cache. Note that this is still a bit experimental so you may hit some bugs -- please let us know if you do. So even if you get 'lahman' and 'hflights', they only have to exist once on your system, yet you will still get the same isolation that Packrat provides. (each unique version of a package gets its own entry in the cache)

Cheers,
Kevin
